question: Ethanoic acid reacts with alcohols to form what compound?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Esters**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Ethanoic acid** reacts with absolute **alcohols** (such as ethanol) in the presence of an **acid catalyst** to produce a compound known as an **Ester**.
 
• This specific chemical reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol is widely known as **Esterification**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Esters.***
 
• In this reaction, the **hydroxyl group (-OH)** of the carboxylic acid is replaced by an **alkoxy group (-OR)** from the alcohol, resulting in the formation of the **ester functional group (-COOR)** and **water** as a byproduct.
 
• Generally, **Concentrated Sulfuric Acid (H2SO4)** is used as a catalyst in this process to accelerate the reaction and act as a dehydrating agent to remove water, shifting the equilibrium toward the product side.
